newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore, Philippine firms in industrial park deal.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, Philippine firms in industrial park deal.

text.p: A joint venture between Singapore and Philippine companies will develop an industrial park just south of Manila, the leading Singapore partner said on Monday.
Jurong Town Corporation International Pte Ltd (JCTI) said the Carmelray Development Corp of the Philippines would hold 60 percent of the joint venture to build the park at Laguna, south of Manila.
JCTI managing director Dominic Ng told a news conference the park was expected to provide about 15,000 jobs after its completion in 1998.
Ng said 30 percent of Carmelray-JCTI Corp joint venture, which planned to spend US$150 on the park's infrastructure, would be owned by three Singapore companies.
JCTI would hold 60 percent of the joint Singapore stake. The rest would be equally divided between Temasek Holdings, the government's investment arm, and Waterbank Properties Pte Ltd.
Industrialists were expected to invest a further US$650 million in the park, Ng said.
"Twelve companies from Singapore, Japan, and the U.S. have expressed strong interest in the site largely from electronics and supporting industries," he said, without identifying them.
"Prices will be competitive with surrounding industrial parks, some quoting from US$150 to US$200 per square km," Ng added.
